domaine-daulny.name: Domaine Daulny
domaine-daulny.line: A family estate in Verdigny, just north of the town of Sancerre, working some fifty small plots across the appellation.
domaine-daulny.tell: Daulny farms about fifty plots around Verdigny and ferments mostly in stainless steel, so the Sancerre is clean Sauvignon Blanc: citrus, gooseberry and a chalky, stony finish. A bright white from the Under $100 page, good with oysters and with fish.

maurice-charleux.name: Domaine Maurice Charleux et Fils
maurice-charleux.line: A family domaine in Dezize-lès-Maranges, founded in 1894, with just under ten hectares of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay at the southern end of the Côte de Beaune.
maurice-charleux.tell: Maranges is the last village of the Côte de Beaune, and La Fussière is its largest premier cru, a south facing slope of limestone over marl. The red is Pinot Noir of red cherry and earth with fresh, firm tannin: a premier cru Burgundy on the Under $100 page, good with duck or veal.

jean-noel-gagnard.name: Domaine Jean-Noël Gagnard
jean-noel-gagnard.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine, farmed organically, known for its whites and for taking the village’s red seriously.
jean-noel-gagnard.tell: Chassagne is known for white, but L’Estimée is red: village Chassagne-Montrachet Pinot Noir blended from six parcels across the commune. Wild strawberry, bright acidity and polished tannin. A chance to show a guest red Chassagne, and a match for roast chicken or pork.

chateau-gloria.name: Château Gloria
chateau-gloria.line: Henri Martin’s Saint-Julien estate, built parcel by parcel from 1942 out of vines bought from the classed growths around it.
chateau-gloria.tell: Gloria was put together long after 1855, from vines Henri Martin bought off Saint-Julien’s classed growths, so it carries no classification; Château Saint-Pierre is its sister. Cabernet Sauvignon leads, with Merlot: cassis, cedar and the village’s fine grained balance. Two vintages at one price, the 2017 with more years in bottle than the 2021.

chateau-la-tour-de-mons.name: Château La Tour de Mons
chateau-la-tour-de-mons.line: An old Margaux estate in the village of Soussans, named for Pierre de Mons, who held it early in the seventeenth century.
chateau-la-tour-de-mons.tell: La Tour de Mons sits in Soussans, at the northern edge of Margaux. Merlot leads the blend, with Cabernet Sauvignon and a little Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot: plum and dark cherry with the appellation’s violet perfume and soft tannin. A Margaux to open with lamb or beef.

chateau-charmail.name: Château Charmail
chateau-charmail.line: A Haut-Médoc estate at Saint-Seurin-de-Cadourne, near the Gironde, its vineyard one block a short way down the road from Sociando-Mallet.
chateau-charmail.tell: Charmail is known in the Médoc for cold macerating its grapes before fermentation, which gives deep colour and soft tannin. Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon lead, with Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. The list prints one bottle, the 2020 in magnum, under Large Formats and again under Bordeaux: a generous claret for a large table.

cru-monplaisir.name: Cru Monplaisir
cru-monplaisir.line: A Bordeaux Supérieur estate just outside the Margaux appellation, bought in 2009 by the Gonet-Médeville family of Champagne.
cru-monplaisir.tell: The list prints Montplasir; the label reads Cru Monplaisir. Two parcels just outside Margaux, below Château Margaux and Château d’Issan, with Merlot leading the two Cabernets: plum, blackcurrant and cedar with soft tannin. A claret with Margaux neighbours at an easy price.

vignobles-levet.name: Vignobles Levet
vignobles-levet.line: A small family estate in Ampuis, farming old vine Syrah on the steep slopes of Côte-Rôtie, in the Côte Brune and La Landonne among others.
vignobles-levet.tell: Levet makes Côte-Rôtie the old way, fermenting with much of the stems and ageing in large casks and demi-muids: dark, earthy, spiced and firm when young. Les Journaries, first made in 2004, comes largely from old vines in La Landonne. Both come in magnum here, and the estate wine also in 2023.

m-chapoutier.name: M. Chapoutier
m-chapoutier.line: A Tain-l’Hermitage house whose history goes back to 1808, farming its own vines biodynamically and printing Braille on its labels.
m-chapoutier.tell: The labels read Les Meysonniers and La Bernardine. Les Meysonniers is Crozes-Hermitage Syrah from the south of the appellation, aged mostly in concrete: raspberry, blackcurrant, round and easy. La Bernardine is Grenache led Châteauneuf-du-Pape with Syrah and Mourvèdre: plum, blackcurrant and spice. Two Rhône reds for lamb or duck.

lemelson.name: Lemelson Vineyards
lemelson.line: A Willamette Valley winery near Carlton, farming its estate vineyards organically in three of the valley’s sub-regions.
lemelson.tell: By the glass, Tikka’s Run is Lemelson’s organic estate Pinot Gris: pear, Meyer lemon, melon and white flowers, fresh with crab or a salad. On the bottle list, Thea’s Selection is the house Pinot Noir, blended from the estate vineyards: red currant, cranberry and a herbal lift, for duck, salmon or pork.

kokomo.name: Kokomo Winery
kokomo.region: Dry Creek Valley, Sonoma County, California
kokomo.line: A Healdsburg winery at Timber Crest Farms in the Dry Creek Valley, making small lots, many from single vineyards, since its first vintage in 2004.
kokomo.tell: By the glass, Kokomo is Sonoma County Cabernet Sauvignon from a small Dry Creek Valley winery, labelled for the county rather than one vineyard. Blackcurrant, dark plum and spice with ripe, firm tannin: a full California Cabernet by the glass, for steak.

la-miraja.name: La Miraja
la-miraja.line: A small family estate in Castagnole Monferrato, in the Asti hills, its cellar in the village’s old castle; Barbera, Grignolino and Ruchè.
la-miraja.tell: By the glass, Le Masche is Barbera d’Asti from the estate’s own vines, all Barbera: dark cherry, plum and Barbera’s bright acidity with soft tannin, good with tomato, pork or mushrooms. The name recalls the masche, spirits of Piedmontese folklore.

patrimony-estate.name: Patrimony
patrimony-estate.line: A Cabernet estate in the Adelaida District of Paso Robles, begun by the brothers who founded DAOU, making Bordeaux style reds of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc.
patrimony-estate.tell: The October list printed these bottles as DAOU; this list prints Patrimony. Patrimony is the estate Cabernet Sauvignon, here in 2018, 2019 and magnum; Caves des Lions blends Cabernet Sauvignon with Cabernet Franc. Soul of a Lion, printed here under Patrimony, is the Cabernet DAOU’s own labels carry. Ripe, dark and polished.
